news.title: Presidenta da Capes será primeira brasileira vice-diretora da Unesco
news.summary: A cientista Denise Pires de Carvalho assumirá nos próximos dias o cargo de Vice Diretora-Geral de Ciências da Organização das Nações Unidas para a Educação, a Ciência e a Cultura (Unesco). É a primeira vez que a cadeira é ocupada pelo Brasil desde a criação da ONU em 1945. Ao fazer a indicação, a Unesco destacou a experiência da cientista em liderança e gestão de pesquisa e avaliação de programas de pesquisa e cooperação científica internacional e afirmou que o trabalho dela “abordou dimensões sociais da ciência, incluindo acesso equitativo, igualdade de gênero e governança institucional inclusiva”. Notícias relacionadas: Trump revoga norma que protegia alunos LGBTI de discriminação sexual . Ataque em escola na Eslováquia deixa pelo menos uma pessoa morta. Preço do petróleo sobe, após Trump rejeitar proposta de paz do Irã. Atual presidente da Coordenação de Aperfeiçoamento de Pessoal de Nível Superior (Capes), Denise afirma que chega à Unesco com o mesmo olhar que o Brasil teve para a ciência nos últimos anos, com reforço do multilateralismo e de uma ciência voltada para as pessoas. “Nesses últimos três anos, o que o Brasil fez, a Capes fez, foi defender a interação sul-sul no nível da pós-graduação, internacionalizar cada vez mais os programas de pós-graduação do país, interagindo com a América Latina e o Caribe, com os países da África, para além de toda a cooperação que nós já fazíamos", disse. Denise também destacou o papel da ciência no desenvolvimento dos países, especialmente os mais pobres. Ela defende que não há saída para o Brasil se tornar um país desenvolvido que não seja através da ciência. “Quem nega a ciência, nega o desenvolvimento da nação. Não há país independente sem universidades. Não há país independente sem ciência. E o Brasil começou muito tardiamente esse processo de verdadeira independência. Todos os países mais desenvolvidos do mundo são mais desenvolvidos porque investiram em ciência”, disse. A Diretoria-Geral para Ciências da Unesco é responsável pela promoção da cooperação científica internacional e pela implementação dos programas da ONU nas áreas de Ciências Naturais e Ciências Sociais e Humanas, incluindo recomendações sobre Ética da Inteligência Artificial. Reconhecimento do Brasil O Ministério de Relações Exteriores do Brasil (MRE) comemorou a indicação e expressou confiança de que a atuação da cientista "contribuirá para fortalecimento das ciências e do seu papel na promoção da paz, da equidade, da sustentabilidade e do desenvolvimento humano”. Quem é Denise Pires de Carvalho Denise Pires de Carvalho é médica com mestrado e doutorado pela Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro, onde também é professora titular do departamento de Biofísica. Em 2019 se tornou a primeira mulher reitora da UFRJ. A cientista atuou também como Secretária de Educação Superior do Ministério da Educação (MEC) entre 2023 e 2024. Em fevereiro de 2024 assumiu a presidência da Capes. Atualmente preside também o Conselho Científico do Institut de Recherche pour le Développement (IRD), da França, e participa de redes de cooperação acadêmica e científica de alcance regional e global.

news.title: Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award
news.summary: French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expansive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.

news.title: A view from Brazil: The fight for the favela vote
news.summary: In Brazil, more than 158 million voters are being called to the polls on Sunday to elect their next president, as well as new members of Congress and governors. In Rio de Janeiro, local candidates are fighting for one particularly sought-after electorate: the residents of favelas. FRANCE 24’s Jan Onoszko reports from Rocinha, Brazil’s largest favela.

news.title: French civil servants strike, demand additional budgetary resources
news.summary: French civil servants were mobilising in large numbers on Tuesday, with more than 170 rallies planned across France. A coalition of unions are demanding additional budgetary resources for schools, hospitals, and other public services. Among those on strike are firefighters, pushed to their limits by the summer's historic wildfires. Here's a look at one of the protests in Lyon.

news.title: Over 100 settlers attack Occupied West Bank village, clash with Israeli forces
news.summary: More than 100 Israeli settlers attacked a village in the north of the occupied West Bank early Tuesday, wounding three members of Israel's security forces and burning two Palestinian homes, authorities and residents said. The attack occurred while the military was attempting to accompany a Palestinian family back to their home in the village of Jalud after they had been displaced by settler attacks two months earlier. ABC Journalist Jordana Miller reports.

news.title: Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit
news.summary: The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.

news.summary: The ban amounts to barely a ripple in $880 billion worth of annual two-way trade between the two northern neighbors. But it marks another ratcheting up of President Donald Trump's second-term trade war with America's longtime ally and trading partner.

news.title: French far-right leader Bardella denies anti-Semitism accusations
news.summary: 🇫🇷 ✡️ Far-right #NationalRally (RN) party leader Jordan #Bardella has denied accusation by French investigative website #Mediapart that he made anti-Semitic comments on private chats in 2013. It comes as RN candidate Marine #LePen is polling well in the lead for the 2027 presidential election.

news.title: France's Le Pen defiant after top ally hit by antisemitism claims
news.summary: French far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen on Tuesday vowed to hit back at allegations of antisemitism targeting her de-facto number two Jordan Bardella, which have punctured her buoyant campaign at a time she is riding high in the polls. Le Pen, who is aiming to win the Elysee at her fourth attempt next year in a far-right breakthrough that would send a shockwave across Europe, lambasted the Mediapart website that published the claims and said Bardella has her "total confidence".

news.title: Calais Jungle: A child and 2 women killed during Channel crossing attempt
news.summary: A 10-year-old child and two women died Monday on the treacherous migration route across the English Channel from France, apparently trampled to death on a boat packed with more than 100 people, French authorities said. The so-called “taxi boat" ran into difficulty off the northern French coast, with its passengers asking for help, authorities said. Such inflatable boats attempt the dangerous crossing after picking up people from the beaches of northern France, where they wade into the sea to clamber aboard. FRANCE 24's Claire Paccalin tells us more.

news.title: Spanish royals welcome French President Macron in official ceremony
news.summary: Spain's King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia welcomed French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte Macron during an official ceremony upon their arrival at Madrid's Royal Palace. French President Macron is on a two-day official visit in Spain. This state visit will serve to highlight and strengthen the ties and bilateral relations between the two countries. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid, Spain.

news.title: OpenAI cancels release of newest model due to safety concerns
news.summary: OpenAI will not release its newest artificial intelligence model, known as Astra 6.1, after internal testing by the ChatGPT-maker revealed it did not meet safety standards, the company confirmed Monday. Concerns about AI safety have escalated in recent months after models developed by OpenAI and rival lab Anthropic were involved in security incidents during testing.

news.title: Can Parisians really teach us to be happier?
news.summary: We welcome back Alex Durand and Tom Carles – better known as AT Frenchies – to talk France, America, friendship and the pursuit of happiness. The childhood friends-turned-internet phenomenon are back with their new book, "Pardon Our French". From growing up together to building a life between France and the US, Alex and Tom share their unique take on what makes Parisians tick, their transatlantic journey, their love of two cultures and the challenges of writing a book together.
